skill.displayName: 商机雷达-比招标更早发现机会

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its business-opportunity purpose, but it adds account registration, device fingerprinting, persistent credentials, signed login-style links, and an unsafe HTML renderer that deserve review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network access is mostly limited to vendor domains and optional WebSearch, but collecting and transmitting a stable MAC-derived hash plus agent metadata is more sensitive than ordinary query submission.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No third-party dependencies or install-time execution were found, and metadata declares ZLBX_API_KEY, but local config/report file access is handled in runtime instructions rather than clearly scoped install metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses many behaviors and requires consent before auto-registration, but the trigger wording is broad, full-mode HTML export runs by default, signed URLs must be output unchanged, and fixed vendor referral content is required in reports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists an API key in ~/.zlbx/config.json and writes reports under ~/zlbx-opportunity-radar-files/, but the credential persistence instructions do not require restrictive permissions, symlink checks, atomic writes, or cleanup of temporary report JSON.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Opportunity search, scoring, reporting, and vendor API use are coherent with the stated purpose, but the artifacts also include automatic account creation, MAC-hash device deduplication, recharge/auto-login link generation, and mandatory preservation of sk signed URLs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this vendor receiving your opportunity-search queries and, if you use automatic registration, a stable MAC-derived device hash. Prefer providing your own ZLBX_API_KEY through a secure environment variable, review any generated sk or auto-login links as sensitive, and avoid sharing exported HTML reports broadly until the link-handling and credential-file protections are improved.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Reading an API key from the environment or ~/.zlbx/config.json and writing reports are expected for this API-backed reporting skill, but the local file authority is under-scoped in metadata.
[TP4] expected: HTML report generation and client-side export are disclosed and fit the reporting purpose; the concern is expanded data handling and the renderer issues, not tool poisoning by itself.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic registration sends platform, architecture, and a deterministic MAC hash to a vendor endpoint; consent is required, but this is a privacy-sensitive account provisioning flow beyond simple opportunity discovery.
[SDI-2] expected: Using ZLBX_API_KEY or ~/.zlbx/config.json is expected for authenticated API access, but the skill directly handles bearer credentials and persists them locally.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The quota-exhaustion flow generates an auto-login recharge SID and points users into account monetization/phone-binding flows, which is payment-adjacent and broader than the core search task.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The requirement to preserve sk signed URL parameters in user-visible output exposes bearer-style links in chat and generated HTML.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The activation language is broader than a narrowly scoped opportunity-search skill and could route adjacent lead/search tasks into this vendor API flow.
[SQP-2] expected: Authenticated X-API-Key requests are necessary for the vendor API, but the instructions lack strong redaction, rotation, and secure-storage handling details.
[E1] unexpected: The external transmission of device-derived registration data is real artifact-backed behavior; it is disclosed and consent-gated, so it supports Review rather than a malicious verdict.
[T01] expected: The hardcoded branding and referral footer are promotional and reduce report neutrality, but they are visibly vendor-branded and not evidence of hidden system or safety hijacking.
[T09] unexpected: The renderer escapes text with xml.sax.saxutils.escape and inserts URLs into double-quoted href attributes without quote escaping or URL validation, allowing unsafe HTML/link injection in generated reports.
[other] unexpected: The MAC-derived hash is a stable device identifier; hashing reduces raw hardware exposure but does not eliminate correlation risk.
